gradingFrame.entryPointNature: `dev` is a LOCAL TESTING entry point: anvil, chain 31337, never broadcast, deploying mock tokens against published Foundry test keys. No finding at this entry point can put a real asset at risk directly, so the High band is structurally unreachable here and was not reached.
gradingFrame.mediumTest: The live question for this run was whether a rehearsal defect reaches Medium. It can: a defect that makes the rehearsal GREEN while the real cutover is BROKEN is a genuine verification-integrity / availability harm, and Medium is the right home for it - BUT ONLY when the causal chain is demonstrated rather than hypothetical. That test was applied individually to DEV26-02 and DEV26-03, the two candidates, and both fail it at the same place: the second link (a real defect that the rehearsal would conceal) is not demonstrated in either case. DEV26-03 disclaims it in its own `notDemonstratedByExecution` field; DEV26-02's demonstrated half stops at a local dev UI. Both hold at Low, with the reasoning recorded per finding under classification.whyNotMedium and an explicit escalationTrigger on DEV26-03.
gradingFrame.severityTracksImpactNotCulpability: Applied in three places, in both directions. (i) DEV26-06: the same-run revocation asymmetry makes the omission look careless, which is culpability - the grant is on a mock token held by a published key, which is the impact, so it stays Low. (ii) DEV26-09: the story-078 contravention and the machine-approved 074/075 closures are governance-process failures, and the code was verified to behave correctly, so it is QA. (iii) The carried-forward chain-guard re-observation (ce524709d965, DEV26-05) arrives with its own severityClassifierNote making the same argument; that entry is a re-observation and is NOT re-graded here - its ledger severity of Low is unchanged and the recommendation to hold rather than escalate is endorsed.
gradingFrame.notDeflatedForBeingATestScript: The inverse error was guarded against too. None of the five was downgraded on the grounds that 'it's only a test script'. All five survived the local-testing rubric on their merits at the sanitizer stage and all five are reported; the Low grades rest on demonstrated blast radius, not on the artifact's status. DEV26-03 is ranked L-01 - first in the report - precisely because its impact ceiling is the highest even though its realised impact today is a coverage gap.
gradingFrame.recallStatement: Law 1: nothing was dropped, merged, or softened at this stage. 5 in, 5 out, 0 removed. Three findings carry flaggedForHumanReview with a stated reason rather than being resolved silently. The one parked item (MR-26-DEV-01, the clean:local rm -rf reaching outside the repo into ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp with an untested forked-anvil branch) is NOT reclassified here and remains in the visible manual-review channel at manual-review.json - it was never a filed finding and this stage does not promote or retire it.

labelingNote: Labels are run-scoped and ordered by severity, then by impact within severity, matching what findings/<sev>/ will hold. L-01 DEV26-03 (highest impact ceiling; headline defect against stated purpose (a)); L-02 DEV26-02 (fully demonstrated concealment, but local blast radius); L-03 DEV26-04 (one unrehearsed UI path); L-04 DEV26-06 (footgun with nil unlocked impact). Q-01 DEV26-09 is the single QA item and ALSO carries spec-conformance label F-01. NO C-XX label was issued this run: DEV26-06 was the only candidate for the Centralization bucket and was placed in Low instead, because no protocol asset sits behind the residual key - calling it a centralization risk would misdescribe a local-chain privilege residue as a trust concentration in the protocol.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: `dev` rehearses the cutover's end state but not its cutover mechanics: setDispatcher, replaceDispatcher and hook.pull() are executed zero times
classifiedFindings.regressionNote: Not a regression. reconciliation.status == 'new'; no ledger entry shares fingerprint eda17642828a, so nothing was previously marked fixed and nothing reappeared.
classifiedFindings.fingerprintProvenance: Copied VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json. Not recomputed, not retyped, not truncated by this stage.
classifiedFindings.description: `DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol` calls `setDispatcher` 9 times, `replaceDispatcher` 9 times and `hook.pull()` at least 3 times. `DeployMocks.s.sol` calls each of them ZERO times. Verified on the live chain: `NFTMinterV2.nextIndex == 8` with `configs[1..7]` each populated exactly once and never repointed — the local chain deploys the post-cutover dispatcher set greenfield, because it has no incumbent to displace. The mainnet script documents the per-index order at `:145-156` — `hook.pull() -> hook.setDispatcher(new) -> new.setHook(hook) -> replaceDispatcher(idx, new)` — and states in its own words that the reverse order 'would put the new dispatcher live on the index while it still carried the fresh DefaultDispatchHook that ATokenDispatcherV2's constructor gave it, so mints would SUCCEED while accruing no mint debt — a silent value leak. Never do that.' The one ordering in the whole cutover whose wrong direction is SILENT rather than loud is the one the local mirror never executes. The same omission also means these mainnet claims are never exercised locally: that `replaceDispatcher` preserves `price`/`growthBasisPoints` (asserted at `:1366-1372` and `:1536`); that `NudgeRatchet._dispatch`'s `hookTypeId() == EXPECTED_HOOK_TYPE_ID` guard holds across a hook reuse; and that `NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook`'s non-default `DEFAULT_RATIO == 100` is not silently reset. Two adjacent cutover behaviours are likewise absent with no analogue: old-batch-minter retirement (`setPauser(OWNER)` + `pause()`), and the story-074 write-once BPT custody baseline / resume-leg handling — the latter structurally un-rehearsable because `DeployMocks` writes `deploymentStatus: "completed"` unconditionally and can never record `in_progress` or `failed`.
classifiedFindings.impact: A reordering regression in the mainnet cutover script — the exact defect class the mainnet script's own comment flags as a silent value leak — would pass the local rehearsal unchanged, because the local rehearsal contains none of the calls involved. The rehearsal's green result therefore carries less assurance than it appears to, which is the concealment bar. No claim is made that the mainnet ordering IS wrong; the finding is that `dev` cannot tell you either way.
classifiedFindings.evidence: grep counts over both scripts (setDispatcher 0 vs 9, replaceDispatcher 0 vs 9); evidence/cast-live-state.log (NFTMinterV2 nextIndex=8, configs[1..7] all greenfield); evidence/dev-script-narrative.log (25 phases, none of them a repoint); reports/.../script-audits/dev/cluster-analysis.md G-1/G-2/G-3
classifiedFindings.crossReference: The unconditional `deploymentStatus: "completed"` write named in the last sentence of the description is itself ledger entry 1e8cc0dc58ba (L-01, open, re-observed STILL-LIVE this run). It is cited here as the CAUSE of one sub-gap, not re-filed. Downstream must not mint a second entry for it.
classifiedFindings.notDemonstratedByExecution: The reverse-order leak was NOT reproduced on the live chain — doing so would have required deploying a fresh six-arg BalancerPoolerV2 plus hook and repointing index 4. The ABSENCE of the calls is proven; the consequence of getting the order wrong is quoted from the mainnet script's own documentation, not independently demonstrated here.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Add a Phase 7.6 to `DeployMocks.s.sol` that, after the greenfield dispatcher set is live, deploys ONE replacement dispatcher and performs a genuine `hook.pull() -> hook.setDispatcher(new) -> new.setHook(hook) -> replaceDispatcher(idx, new)` on a single index, asserting (i) mint-debt conservation across the swap, (ii) `price`/`growthBasisPoints` preserved, and (iii) that a mint attempted in the intermediate window REVERTS rather than succeeding. One index is sufficient to make the ordering executable and therefore regression-testable. Separately, run `VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol` (story 075) against the local end state — it is free there, and story 075 closed via machine approval with its own declared regression gate never run.
classifiedFindings.recommendationProvenance: VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json, byte-for-byte. Non-empty verified.

classification.c4Definition: QA/Low — 'state handling, function incorrect as to spec'. A test/rehearsal-coverage gap in a non-deployed local script.
classification.assetImpact: None. `dev` never broadcasts (anvil, chain 31337) and holds no value. The mainnet script it fails to rehearse was not shown to be defective.
classification.functionOrAvailabilityImpact: None today. The protocol's function and availability are unchanged by a gap in a local rehearsal. What is degraded is *verification assurance*: the local green result carries less signal than it appears to.
impactChain: 1. DeployMocks.s.sol deploys the post-cutover dispatcher set greenfield (verified on-chain: NFTMinterV2.nextIndex==8, configs[1..7] populated once, never repointed).
2. Therefore setDispatcher / replaceDispatcher / hook.pull() execute 0x locally vs 9x / 9x / 3+ on DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol. ABSENCE IS PROVEN.

3. The mainnet script documents `pull -> setDispatcher -> setHook -> replaceDispatcher` and warns the reverse order is SILENT ('mints would SUCCEED while accruing no mint debt - a silent value leak. Never do that.').
4. CONDITIONAL, NOT DEMONSTRATED: *if* a future edit reorders that sequence, the local rehearsal would still pass, because it contains none of the calls involved.
5. Realised harm today: reduced assurance from a passing rehearsal. No value moves, nothing is unavailable, no attacker is involved.
classification.likelihood: n/a - no attack path exists. The exposure is a latent detection gap, not an exploitable condition.
classification.assumptions: That a reordering regression could be introduced into DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol in future. No such regression exists at e1db0f1.
classification.externalRequirements: A future code change to the mainnet cutover script that no one reviews by hand.
classification.attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
classification.localScriptRubric: KEEP, and this is the rubric's central case: the greenfield shortcut is admissible in itself, but it removes the one cutover mechanic whose failure mode is silent from the rehearsal entirely.
classification.lawNotes: Law 1: recall preserved - fully reported, not suppressed, and flagged as the headline defect against the requester's stated purpose (a). Not a Law-2 item (no story requires the rehearsal).
classification.whyNotMedium: Considered seriously and rejected. C4 Medium requires protocol function/availability impact OR a value leak with a stated attack path. Here the value leak belongs to a DIFFERENT artifact (the mainnet script) and was explicitly NOT reproduced - the finding proves only the absence of the calls. Grading the untested script at the severity of the bug it might one day fail to catch would (a) charge this finding for a defect nobody has shown to exist, and (b) collide head-on with the C4 known-invalid class 'speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause'. Missing test coverage is Low/QA under C4 even when what is untested is high-risk. Holding Low is not report-tidying: the finding is reported in full, at the top of the Low bucket, with its whole narrative and the mainnet script's own warning quoted.
classification.escalationTrigger: This becomes Medium-or-higher the moment someone demonstrates an actual ordering defect (or a hook/price/growthBasisPoints regression) in DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol. That would be a NEW finding at the promotion-ready entry point, not a re-grade of this one. Recommend the next promotion-ready audit carry this as an explicit hypothesis to test.

classifiedFindings.rationale: Highest-impact-ceiling finding of the run, but it is a coverage gap, not a defect: no deployed code is wrong, no asset is at risk, and the finding's own `notDemonstratedByExecution` disclaims that the mainnet ordering IS wrong. The Medium test fails at its first link.
classifiedFindings.humanReviewReason: Borderline Low/Medium. Documented above under whyNotMedium; a reviewer who believes the mainnet cutover's untested silent-leak path is itself an availability risk to the imminent cutover may argue Medium. Classifier's position is Low on demonstrated impact.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.title: clean:local deletes the JSON deployment artifacts but leaves addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts stale, so the in-repo consumer fails loudly while the external UI consumer fails silently
classifiedFindings.regressionNote: Not a regression. reconciliation.status == 'new'; no ledger entry shares fingerprint ec29eacd9501, so nothing was previously marked fixed and nothing reappeared.
classifiedFindings.fingerprintProvenance: Copied VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json. Not recomputed, not retyped, not truncated by this stage.
classifiedFindings.description: `clean:local` is `rm -rf broadcast/*/31337 server/deployments/progress.31337.json server/deployments/local.json && rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*`. It does NOT delete `server/deployments/addresses.ts` or `server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` — the two TypeScript artifacts the external UI repo actually imports. On any chain that aborts after the clean (and the clean runs first in both job 1 and again inside `deploy:local`), the workspace is left with NO JSON and STALE TypeScript. Demonstrated empirically: after running `clean:local` against a completed deployment, `progress.31337.json` and `local.json` were gone and `broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337` was removed, while `local-addresses.ts` was byte-identical (sha256 prefix c8e0355fbc73, unchanged) and still named `PhlimboV3: "0xC32609C91d6B6b51D48f2611308FEf121B02041f"`. The asymmetry is the finding, and it runs the wrong way round: the JSON consumers inside this repo fail LOUDLY and correctly — `server/index.js` re-reads both files on every request, so `/health` honestly flipped to `deploymentsLoaded:false` and `/contracts` returned HTTP 404 — but the TypeScript consumer, which is the external UI repo and therefore the entire point of stated purpose (b), has no staleness signal whatsoever. It simply imports addresses for contracts that no longer exist on any chain.
classifiedFindings.impact: A developer whose `npm run dev` aborted mid-chain, or who re-cleaned without redeploying, has a UI that builds and runs against addresses from a previous anvil session. On a fresh anvil those addresses are code-less; on a re-run they are frequently the same deterministic CREATE addresses for a DIFFERENT deployment generation, which is worse — the UI appears to work while reading a contract that is not the one it thinks it is. This is the concealment case the local-testing framing does not excuse.
classifiedFindings.evidence: evidence/clean-local-stale-ts-demo.log (before/after sha256 of all four artifacts, plus the /health and /contracts responses)
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Add `server/deployments/addresses.ts server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` to the `clean:local` rm list, so an aborted run leaves nothing rather than something stale. If the .ts files must survive for editor tooling, instead have `generate:ts-anvil` stamp a run id (block hash or timestamp) into both files and have the UI bootstrap assert it against `GET /health` — but deletion is simpler and fails in the safe direction.
classifiedFindings.recommendationProvenance: VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json, byte-for-byte. Non-empty verified.

classification.c4Definition: QA/Low — incorrect state handling in a build/lifecycle script; a partial clean that leaves a stale artifact.
classification.assetImpact: None. `local-addresses.ts` / `addresses.ts` are generated from anvil state; `clean:local` does not touch the hand-maintained `mainnet-addresses.ts`. No mainnet contract, balance, or user is reachable from this defect.
classification.functionOrAvailabilityImpact: None to the protocol. Degrades the local dev loop: the external UI builds and runs against addresses from a dead deployment generation with no staleness signal.
impactChain: 1. `clean:local` rm's broadcast/*/31337, progress.31337.json and local.json but NOT addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts.
2. DEMONSTRATED (evidence/clean-local-stale-ts-demo.log): after a clean, both .ts files are byte-identical (sha256 prefix c8e0355fbc73) and still name PhlimboV3 at 0xC32609C9...
3. The in-repo JSON consumers fail LOUDLY and correctly - /health flips deploymentsLoaded:false, /contracts returns HTTP 404.
4. The external UI, which imports the .ts files, has NO staleness signal - the asymmetry runs the wrong way round.

5. On a fresh anvil the stale addresses are code-less (fails, if noisily); on a re-run, deterministic CREATE frequently reproduces the SAME address for a DIFFERENT deployment generation, so the UI reads a live-but-wrong contract and shows no error. This is the concealment case.
6. Realised harm: misattributed UI bugs and lost developer time, bounded to the local machine.
classification.likelihood: High as an occurrence (any aborted `npm run dev`, any re-clean without redeploy), low as a harm (surfaces the moment the developer exercises anything stateful).
classification.assumptions: Developer re-runs or aborts mid-chain without a full redeploy.
classification.attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
classification.localScriptRubric: KEEP - demonstrated concealment against the external UI consumer, which is the whole of stated purpose (b).
classification.lawNotes: Law 1: the concealment mechanism is the reason it is kept rather than filtered as a transparently-local shortcut.
classification.whyNotMedium: The silent-wrong-contract mechanism is the strongest Medium argument in the run and it is genuinely demonstrated, not hypothesised. It still falls short: the affected consumer is a local development UI on chain 31337, so nothing the protocol does becomes unavailable and no value can leak. A Medium here would rest on the same two-step 'a UI bug might therefore ship' conditional as DEV26-03, and the second step is undemonstrated. Low, ranked immediately below L-01.

classifiedFindings.rationale: A real, empirically demonstrated defect with a genuine silent-failure mechanism, but its entire blast radius is one developer's local session: the stale artifacts are the LOCAL address book on chain 31337, and no protocol asset or availability is touched.

classifiedFindings.label: L-03
classifiedFindings.title: The local chain arms a Kendu promotion that story 076 asserts must be dormant on mainnet, and never produces the dormant state the UI will actually ship against
classifiedFindings.regressionNote: Not a regression. reconciliation.status == 'new'; no ledger entry shares fingerprint 12bcca3b617c, so nothing was previously marked fixed and nothing reappeared.
classifiedFindings.fingerprintProvenance: Copied VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json. Not recomputed, not retyped, not truncated by this stage.
classifiedFindings.description: `_armLocalKenduPromotion` arms a 10,000-Kendu / 1-day promotion on PhlimboV3. Verified live: `promoToken == MockKendu`, `promoPhase == Active (1)`, `promoRewardBalance == 10,000e18`, `promoRewardPerSecond == 1.157e35`. Story 076 asserts the exact opposite for mainnet — `promoToken == address(0)`, Kendu deliberately unset, Phase 7 asserting the negative — and `DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol` calls `startPromotion` nowhere. THE ARMING ITSELF IS ADMISSIBLE and is not the finding: it is declared deliberate at `:183-198`, argued well (with no promotion running, every new V3 UI field — 13/16/17/18/19 plus the three unclaimable banks on DepositPageViewV3 — reads zero, which is indistinguishable from a broken binding), and carefully sequenced dead-last so the migrator's `promoToken`-delta path stays dormant during the migration. The finding is the INVERSE: because the promotion is armed unconditionally at the end of every local run, no local run ever produces the DORMANT promo state that mainnet will actually ship on day one. The UI's dormant-promotion rendering path is the one path `dev` never exercises, and it is the path that goes live first. Compounding it, `mainnet-addresses.ts` carries `Kendu: "0x000…0"` (see ledger 3177eed94ecb), so a UI developer working against `dev` sees an active promotion on a live Kendu token where mainnet will present a dormant promotion on the zero address. Note per project policy that the in-source comment declaring this deliberate is evidence of intent, not suppression authority.
classifiedFindings.impact: The day-one mainnet UI state — dormant promo, zero-address Kendu — is the single state the local rehearsal cannot produce, so any rendering bug specific to it (a zero-division on `promoRewardPerSecond`, a null-token symbol lookup, a banner that renders 'promotion active' off a non-zero `promoPhase` enum) ships unrehearsed. This is a purpose-(b) blind spot created by an otherwise-sound purpose-(b) shortcut.
classifiedFindings.evidence: evidence/live-state-fork-test.log (test_B: promoToken/promoPhase/promoBalance read live); evidence/dev-script-narrative.log (the four require-based post-conditions at :1913-1916 all passing); DeployMocks.s.sol:183-198 and :1902-1921
classifiedFindings.crossReference: The `Kendu: 0x0` half of the compounding argument is ledger entry 3177eed94ecb (re-observed this run as DEV26-01, collapsed). Cited, not re-filed.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Make both promo states reachable locally. Cheapest: gate the call on an env flag (`LOCAL_PROMO=off` skips `_armLocalKenduPromotion`) so a developer can boot the dormant chain on demand. Better: add a follow-on local phase that ends the promotion after arming it, so a single `npm run dev` produces the armed state AND leaves a documented one-command path to the dormant/depleted state. Either way, keep the four non-vacuous post-condition requires — they are correct and should not be relaxed.
classifiedFindings.recommendationProvenance: VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json, byte-for-byte. Non-empty verified.

classification.c4Definition: QA/Low — rehearsal state deviates from the stated mainnet end state; a coverage gap on one UI rendering path.
classification.assetImpact: None. Local mock Kendu, local promotion, chain 31337.
classification.functionOrAvailabilityImpact: None to the protocol. The day-one mainnet UI state (dormant promo, Kendu at 0x0) is the one state `dev` cannot produce, so any rendering bug specific to it ships unrehearsed.
impactChain: 1. `_armLocalKenduPromotion` arms a 10,000-Kendu / 1-day promo unconditionally at the end of EVERY local run (verified live: promoToken==MockKendu, promoPhase==Active(1), balance 10,000e18, rate 1.157e35).
2. Story 076 asserts the opposite for mainnet (promoToken==address(0)); DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol calls startPromotion nowhere.

3. THE ARMING IS ADMISSIBLE and is not the filed defect - it is declared deliberate at :183-198, well argued (at zero, an unarmed slot and a broken binding are indistinguishable) and sequenced dead-last so the migrator's promoToken-delta path stays dormant.
4. FILED DEFECT: no local run reaches the dormant state, so the UI path that goes live FIRST on mainnet is the one path never exercised.

5. Compounded by mainnet-addresses.ts carrying Kendu at 0x0 (ledger 3177eed94ecb, cited not re-filed): the dev-chain developer sees an active promo on a live token where mainnet shows a dormant promo on the zero address.
6. Realised harm: a zero-division on promoRewardPerSecond, a null-symbol lookup, or a 'promotion active' banner driven off a non-zero enum could ship unrehearsed. None demonstrated.
classification.likelihood: n/a - no attack path. Detection gap only.
classification.assumptions: That the UI has a dormant-promo rendering path whose correctness is not otherwise verified.
classification.attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
classification.localScriptRubric: KEEP - 'shows the UI/operator a state mainnet will not produce', and its converse.
classification.lawNotes: Law 2 adjacent (the rehearsal inverts a story-076 mainnet invariant) but NOT tagged faithfulness: story 076 scopes itself to mainnet script/src and the divergence is declared and deliberate. The unreachable-inverse defect is a coverage issue, not a story deviation. Faithfulness routing for this run belongs to Q-01/F-01.
classification.whyNotMedium: A single unrehearsed front-end rendering path, with no demonstrated rendering bug behind it, is not protocol function or availability impact. The in-source comment declaring the arming deliberate is treated as evidence of intent with no suppression authority - correctly, since it does not address the inverse - but that does not raise severity either.

classifiedFindings.rationale: Correctly filed as the INVERSE of an admissible shortcut: the arming is fine, the unreachability of the dormant state is the defect. Impact is one unrehearsed UI rendering path - no assets, no protocol function.

classifiedFindings.label: L-04
classifiedFindings.title: The deploy script grants itself phUSD mint authority and never revokes it, while correctly revoking PhlimboV2's grant in the same run
classifiedFindings.regressionNote: Not a regression. reconciliation.status == 'new'; no ledger entry shares fingerprint b8e3d59139ae, so nothing was previously marked fixed and nothing reappeared.
classifiedFindings.footgunClass: non-obvious owner footgun / operational hazard (Law 3). NOT a malicious-owner vector; none is asserted anywhere in the finding.
classifiedFindings.fingerprintProvenance: Copied VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json. Not recomputed, not retyped, not truncated by this stage.
classifiedFindings.description: `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` is granted at `:1784`, `:2025` and `:2122` and is never revoked. Verified live at the end of the run: `phUSD.authorizedMinters(0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266) == (true, 1)`. The grant is a legitimate local shortcut — the deployer acts as a synthetic donor to seed the phUSD nudge stream, which story 073 sanctions — and the token is a mock on a chain whose keys are public, so there is no local risk. The finding is the inconsistency and what it costs the rehearsal: the SAME script, in the SAME run, correctly revokes PhlimboV2's grant as an explicit ordered step of the Phase 7.4 wind-down (verified: `authorizedMinters(PhlimboV2) == (false, 1)`, `authorizedMinters(PhlimboV3) == (true, 1)`), and logs it as such. So privilege revocation is clearly understood as a first-class cutover step here — just not applied to the deployer's own grant. Consequently the local chain's end state carries a live minter that mainnet's end state must not, and the 'revoke the operational key's temporary grant' step is never rehearsed even though it is precisely the kind of step that is easy to forget on a Ledger broadcast.
classifiedFindings.impact: No local risk (mock token, public anvil key). The cost is rehearsal fidelity: a residual-privilege sweep is never exercised, and the local end state differs from the intended mainnet end state in a way no assertion catches. This is an owner footgun of the non-obvious kind — the script's own careful revocation of the OTHER grant makes it read as though residual privileges were swept.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Revoke the deployer's grant at the end of `run()` with `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, false)` and assert it, mirroring the Phase 7.4 wind-down's own pattern. Better still, add a terminal 'residual privilege sweep' phase that asserts the full expected end-state ACL — deployer not a minter, PhlimboV2 not a minter, PhlimboV3 a minter — so the check is declarative and a future grant that forgets to clean up fails the run.
classifiedFindings.recommendationProvenance: VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json, byte-for-byte. Non-empty verified.

classification.c4Definition: QA/Low — access-control end state / operational hazard. Considered for the Centralization (C-01) bucket and rejected: no protocol asset sits behind the residual key, so labelling it a centralization risk would misdescribe it.
classification.assetImpact: None. The grant is on a MOCK phUSD, on chain 31337, to anvil key #0 (0xf39Fd6...2266) whose private key is published in Foundry's own documentation. There is no path from this grant to the real phUSD: DeployMocks deploys its own mock token, so even a mis-targeted run could not grant against the live minter ACL.
classification.functionOrAvailabilityImpact: None. The cost is that the 'revoke the operational key's temporary grant' step - exactly the step easiest to forget on a Ledger broadcast - is never rehearsed, and no assertion would catch its omission.
impactChain: 1. phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true) at :1784, :2025, :2122; never revoked. Verified live: authorizedMinters(0xf39Fd6...2266)==(true,1).
2. The grant itself is a sanctioned local shortcut (story 073): the deployer acts as synthetic donor to seed the phUSD nudge stream.

3. THE FOOTGUN: the SAME script in the SAME run explicitly revokes PhlimboV2's grant as a logged, ordered step of the Phase 7.4 wind-down (verified: PhlimboV2==(false,1), PhlimboV3==(true,1)) while leaving its own grant live.

4. SURPRISE TEST MET: a competent, non-malicious operator reading that careful wind-down would reasonably conclude the ACL had been swept. The asymmetry is the evidence it was an oversight, not a decision.
5. Realised harm: local end state carries a live minter the intended mainnet end state must not, and the residual-privilege sweep is absent from the rehearsal. No value at risk anywhere.
classification.likelihood: Certain to occur (unconditional, every run); zero consequence on the local chain.
classification.assumptions: None for the observed state. The concern is transfer of the omission pattern to a broadcast context, which is not demonstrated.
classification.externalRequirements: For any real risk, the pattern would have to recur in a mainnet broadcast script against the real phUSD - not observed at e1db0f1.
classification.attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.

classifiedFindings.description: LAW-2 FINDING, STATED PLAINLY. `script/DeployMocks.s.sol` references 'Story 079' ten times and `script/interactions/AddressLoader.sol` once more. Globbing the entire phStaging2 story tree across all state folders (`complete`, `incomplete`, `review`, `auto-complete`) for `079-*.md` and `079.*-*.md` returns ZERO hits; the highest existing phStaging2 story is 078. The only 079 anywhere under the stories tree belongs to a different project and is unrelated. Every occurrence was introduced by head commit `e1db0f1`, which is itself UNTAGGED (no `[story-NNN]` prefix); the delta base `3fb4e34` contains none. The work so attributed is the whole subject of this audit — the Phase 7.4 PhlimboV2→V3 cutover rehearsal, the local-only Kendu promotion, the keyless DepositPageViewV3 registration, the AddressLoader rewrite. It is also covered by no story that DOES exist: 076 and 077 scope themselves to mainnet `script/`/`src/` and never mention DeployMocks, and 078 explicitly instructs 'Do not modify `DeployMocks.s.sol`.' Related metadata flag: four of the seven closure stories closed via an undocumented `auto-complete` state carrying 'Approved by: story-batch workflow (machine approval — not human-reviewed)', including BOTH audit-remediation stories 074 and 075, and story 075's own declared primary regression gate (`npm run promotion-ready:dry`) was never run. IMPORTANTLY, this is a provenance gap and not a correctness gap: the work was verified to behave correctly on its own terms — stake conserved 300e18 through a chunked two-pass migration, V2 drained to 0, mint authority moved V2→V3, the two-step APY latch committed on both, the promo armed with four non-vacuous read-back requires, and DepositPageViewV3 registered and returning a live 23-field tuple. The code is unusually well commented and argues each divergence in place.
classifiedFindings.impact: No behavioural impact. The cost is that a substantial, deliberately-divergent change to the project's only cutover rehearsal cannot be graded for story-faithfulness by anyone — including a future audit — because no acceptance criteria exist, and one story in scope actively forbids the change that was made. Under Law 2 that is reportable in itself.
